proof.text: Apply the projective-model statement to the simplicial-set model category and the small simplicial categories $\mathfrak C[A]$ and $\mathfrak C[B]$. Its projective structures have objectwise weak equivalences and fibrations, and evaluation sends projectively cofibrant-fibrant diagrams to cofibrant-fibrant values. Hence every value $F(a)$ is bifibrant. Restriction gives $D(b)=F(u(b))$, so every value of $D$ is bifibrant; since the map $D\to *$ is objectwise a fibration, $D$ is projectively fibrant.

proof.text: Factor $\varnothing\to D$ functorially as the projective cofibration $\varnothing\to QD$ followed by the projective trivial fibration $a:QD\to D$. The first map makes $QD$ cofibrant. By Step 1, $D\to *$ is a projective fibration, so the composite $QD\to D\to *$ is a fibration and $QD$ is fibrant. Because projective weak equivalences are objectwise, $a$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence.

source.place: Theorem 2.2.1.2 and Proposition A.3.3.2 (functorial projective factorization).

proof.text: Use the localized-evaluation comparison for $K=A$ and $K=B$. It supplies $E_K$ with $E_Kq_K\simeq e_K$, identifies its restriction to projectively cofibrant-fibrant diagrams with the enriched-evaluation comparison $\Phi_K$, and says that an objectwise weak equivalence of Kan-valued diagrams induces an equivalence under $e_K$. Thus $e_B(a):e_B(QD)\to e_B(D)$ is an equivalence. The evaluation-restriction statement, applied with $K=A$, $K'=B$, $v=u$ and $P=F$, gives the exact identity $e_B(D)=e_B(u^*F)=e_A(F)\circ u$ on every simplex, including its operators (directly: $N_{\mathrm{hc}}(F\circ\mathfrak C[u])\eta_B=N_{\mathrm{hc}}(F)\eta_Au$ by naturality of the unit $\eta$). Since $QD$ is projectively cofibrant-fibrant, the two identifications with $E_K$ are $\Phi_B$ and $\Phi_A$, yielding $\Phi_B(QD)\simeq\Phi_A(F)\circ u$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.4.4 and the localized enriched-evaluation construction.

proof.text: Apply the evaluation-restriction statement with $K=A$, $K'=B$, $v=u$, and with the ordinary functorial projective cofibrant replacement $Q_B$ given by the functorial factorization of Step 2, restricted to $\mathsf D_B^f$, with its natural trivial fibration $a_B:Q_B\to1$; that statement assumes no simplicial enrichment of $Q_B$ and allows $Q_B(u^*P)\to u^*P$ for $u^*P=D$. It states that $u^*$ preserves objectwise Kan diagrams and $W$ and induces $\overline{u^*}:\mathcal L_A\to\mathcal L_B$; that the identity $e_B(u^*P)=e_A(P)u$ induces a coherent natural equivalence $E_B\overline{u^*}\simeq u^*E_A$; that these comparisons are jointly coherent for identity maps, composites of indexing maps, ordinary diagram transformations and all higher simplices of the infinity localizations; and that the replacement equivalences $e_B(a_B)$, through $E_Bq_B\simeq e_B$, are coherently compatible with restriction and independent of the replacement. The equivalence of Step 3 is the composite of $E_Bq_B(QD)\simeq e_B(QD)$, of $e_B(a_B)$ at $D$, of the comparison $E_B\overline{u^*}\simeq u^*E_A$ at $q_AF$, and of $E_Aq_A\simeq e_A$ at the cofibrant-fibrant $F$, where the last and first are the identifications with $\Phi_A(F)$ and $\Phi_B(QD)$. Each factor is one of these coherent comparisons, so the equivalence is a coherent transformation in the functor quasicategory $\operatorname{Fun}(B,\mathcal S_{\mathcal V})$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], natural in $F$ after localization including transformations and higher simplices; for composable $w:C\to B$ and $u$, joint coherence for composites makes the comparison for $uw$ the composite of the comparisons for $w$ and $u$, and for $u$ an identity the comparison is the replacement equivalence alone.

The covariant part of the right-fibration presentation defines $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$ on projective simplicial diagrams, with left-fibration values. It states that $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_S$ preserves objectwise weak equivalences between objectwise Kan diagrams and that for every map $u:B\to A$ there is a natural base-change isomorphism $u^*U^{\mathrm{cov}}_A(F)\cong U^{\mathrm{cov}}_B(F\circ\mathfrak C[u])$, compatible with composition. Apply this to the objectwise weak equivalence $a:QD\to D$ from Step 2. It gives an equivalence $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_B(QD)\to U^{\mathrm{cov}}_B(D)$ of left fibrations; composing with the base-change isomorphism identifies the target with $u^*U^{\mathrm{cov}}_A(F)$ and proves the final assertion.

title: Derived restriction and coherent evaluation for projective diagrams
statement: Use simplicial sets and coherent functors of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], the coherent realization, projective model structures and covariant unstraightening $U^{\mathrm{cov}}$ of [lem-coef-simplicial-right-fibration-presentation], and the enriched-evaluation rectification comparison of [lem-coef-enriched-diagram-rectification], in fixed sufficiently large universes. Let $u:B\to A$ be a map of small simplicial sets and let $F:\mathfrak C[A]\to\mathsf{sSet}$ be a projectively cofibrant-fibrant simplicial functor. Put $D=F\circ\mathfrak C[u]$. Functorially factor $\varnothing\to D$ as a projective cofibration $\varnothing\to QD$ followed by a projective trivial fibration $QD\to D$. Then $QD$ is cofibrant-fibrant and $QD\to D$ is an objectwise weak homotopy equivalence. If $\Phi_A$ and $\Phi_B$ denote the enriched-evaluation rectification comparisons, there is a coherent equivalence $\Phi_B(QD)\simeq\Phi_A(F)\circ u$, natural in $F$ and $u$ after localization, including their transformations and higher simplices and compatible with composition of base maps. The map $U^{\mathrm{cov}}_B(QD)\to U^{\mathrm{cov}}_B(D)\cong u^*U^{\mathrm{cov}}_A(F)$ is an equivalence of left fibrations over $B$.
